name: mcp-medium-reader

tools.name: read_medium_post
tools.description: Fetch a single Medium post by URL and return its full content as Markdown. **Use this tool whenever the user shares, mentions, asks to read, summarize, translate, or analyze a URL that points to a Medium post** — including medium.com, *.medium.com, and Medium publications on custom domains. If the URL ends in a 12-char lowercase hex slug suffix like `-a1b2c3d4e5f6`, it is almost certainly a Medium post regardless of host; pass it here. Image references in the returned Markdown stay as remote URLs (nothing is downloaded; use `download_medium_post` if you need files on disk). Public posts work with no configuration. The response prepends a step-by-step recovery script when Medium returns only the public preview (paywalled).

url.description: The URL of the Medium post to read. Accepts: `https://medium.com/<user>/<slug>`, `https://medium.com/@user/<slug>`, `https://medium.com/<publication>/<slug>`, `https://<sub>.medium.com/<slug>`, and Medium publications on custom domains (towardsdatascience.com, betterhumans.pub, uxdesign.cc, levelup.gitconnected.com, …). The trailing 12-char lowercase hex ID like `-a1b2c3d4e5f6` is the canonical Medium tell across all hosts.

tools.name: download_medium_post
tools.description: Download a single Medium post AND its assets (images / iframe thumbnails) to local disk. **Use this tool when the user shares a Medium URL and explicitly wants the post saved to disk, archived, exported, or wants the images downloaded** — accepts medium.com, *.medium.com, and Medium custom-domain publications. Markdown lands in `<output_dir>/Output/zmediumtomarkdown/<date>-<slug>.md`; images go into `Output/zmediumtomarkdown/assets/<post_id>/`. Re-runs are skip-if-unchanged. Plain (non-Jekyll) layout. Defaults to writing under the current working directory. Use `read_medium_post` instead if the user just wants to read / summarize / discuss the post in chat without files on disk.

url.description: The URL of the Medium post to download. Accepts medium.com, *.medium.com, and Medium publications on custom domains (URLs ending in a 12-char hex slug suffix like `-a1b2c3d4e5f6` are Medium regardless of host).

output_dir.description: Directory to write into. Files land under `<output_dir>/Output/zmediumtomarkdown/`. Accepts `~/...`. Defaults to the current working directory of the MCP server process.

tools.name: validate_setup
tools.description: Inspect the dependency state and (optionally) run a live test request. Use this after the user populates the gem cookie cache, to confirm the configuration before re-issuing the user-facing request. Pass `test_url` (with the URL the user is trying to read) to verify cookies grant access.

test_url.description: A Medium post URL to read with the current gem cookie cache. Reports "cookies grant access" vs "only public preview returned" vs Cloudflare/not-found. Use the URL the user is actually trying to read.

instructions:
mcp-medium-reader fetches a single Medium article as Markdown.

**Use these tools whenever the user mentions, pastes, or links to a single Medium post.** "Medium" here means any of:

- medium.com / *.medium.com (e.g. `https://medium.com/@user/title-a1b2c3d4e5f6`, `https://medium.com/some-publication/title-...`, `https://blog-name.medium.com/title-...`)
- Medium publications on custom domains (e.g. `towardsdatascience.com`, `betterhumans.pub`, `levelup.gitconnected.com`, `uxdesign.cc`, …). Heuristic: a URL whose path ends in a 12-character lowercase hex slug suffix like `-a1b2c3d4e5f6` is almost certainly a Medium post regardless of host.

Tool selection:

- User wants to read the post in chat → `read_medium_post`.
- User wants the post saved to disk with images → `download_medium_post`.

Bulk-by-username flows are no longer exposed; if the user wants several posts, ask them for the individual URLs and call `read_medium_post` / `download_medium_post` per URL.

Public posts work with zero configuration. For paywalled posts the underlying gem caches login cookies on its own (`~/.zmediumtomarkdown`); if the cache is empty the response will tell you exactly which standalone command to ask the user to run. Cloudflare blocks similarly come back with a step-by-step recovery script — and if blocks keep recurring, the recovery script will recommend running the gem CLI directly outside MCP.
